description.summary: Slender Man is a fictional supernatural character created by Eric Knudsen ('Victor Surge') on the Something Awful forums on June 10, 2009. He is depicted as an unnaturally tall, thin, faceless figure in a black suit and is one of the foundational figures of digital folklore.
description.full: Slender Man is a fictional supernatural entity that originated as an internet creation on the Something Awful forum 'Create Paranormal Images' Photoshop contest. On June 10, 2009, user Eric Knudsen (forum name 'Victor Surge') posted two black-and-white photographs in which a tall, thin figure in a black suit had been added to images of children, with brief invented witness-account captions. The character rapidly proliferated across the internet, becoming the central figure of an early-2010s wave of collaborative horror fiction known as creepypasta. Slender Man is depicted as unnaturally tall and thin, with a featureless white face, a black suit, and tentacle-like appendages, and is associated with the stalking and abduction of children. Major fictional treatments include the Marble Hornets web series (2009–2014), the video games Slender: The Eight Pages (2012) and Slender: The Arrival (2013), the HBO documentary Beware the Slenderman (2016), and the 2018 feature film Slender Man. The character is widely studied as an example of digital folklore (e.g., Trevor J. Blank, Andrew Peck). A 2014 stabbing in Waukesha, Wisconsin, in which two 12-year-old girls attacked a classmate and cited Slender Man, generated extensive moral-panic coverage and academic analysis.

etymology.origin: Coined by Eric Knudsen ('Victor Surge') on the Something Awful forum, June 10, 2009.
etymology.meaning: Descriptive — a 'slender' (tall and thin) figure in human form.
etymology.first_use: June 10, 2009, in the Something Awful 'Create Paranormal Images' thread.

features.description: A blank, smooth, white head with no eyes, nose, or mouth
Often depicted at 2.4–4.5 m (8–15 ft) tall with elongated, spindly proportions
Almost always depicted in a black suit and tie
Black tentacles or extra limbs extending from the back, depicted in many fan works

physical.morphology: Humanoid in basic form but exaggerated to the point of impossibility — extreme height, elongated limbs, and a blank face make him uncanny rather than literal.

abilities.description: Frequently appears and disappears without warning in stories and games
Said to cause paranoia, nightmares, memory loss, nosebleeds, and coughing in those who become aware of him
Described as silently stalking, abducting, and traumatising victims, especially children
In Marble Hornets and related fiction, controls human 'proxies' who do his bidding

behavior.diet: Not specified; primarily framed as a predator that abducts rather than literally feeds
patterns: Visible in the background of photographs (the originating Knudsen images)
Often appears to those who research him too deeply (in-fiction)

range.description: As an internet-native fictional entity, Slender Man's 'distribution' is global wherever the anglophone internet reaches. The originating community is North American, but the character has become a globally recognised piece of digital folklore.

origins.cultural_roots: Slender Man is unambiguously a 21st-century internet creation; his 'lore' was assembled in real time by online communities through collaborative photo manipulation, fictional first-person accounts, and ARG-style web series.
origins.earliest_accounts: June 10, 2009 Photoshop-contest posts by Eric Knudsen.
origins.folklore_connections: Treated by folklorists (Trevor J. Blank, Andrew Peck, Lynne S. McNeill) as a paradigm case of 'digital folklore' or 'networked folklore'.

timeline.event: Eric Knudsen ('Victor Surge') posts the first two Slender Man images on Something Awful's 'Create Paranormal Images' thread
timeline.source: Something Awful forum archives; Wikipedia, 'Slender Man'

timeline.event: The Marble Hornets web series begins on YouTube, expanding the character into video
timeline.significance: Establishes the most influential fictional treatment

timeline.event: Slender: The Eight Pages is released by Mark J. Hadley
timeline.significance: Brings Slender Man into mainstream gaming

timeline.event: Two 12-year-old girls (Morgan Geyser and Anissa Weier) stab a classmate 19 times in Waukesha, Wisconsin, and later cite Slender Man as motivation
timeline.significance: The 'Slender Man stabbing'; becomes a focal moral-panic event
timeline.source: Waukesha County Court records; HBO Beware the Slenderman (2016)

timeline.event: Beware the Slenderman, directed by Irene Taylor Brodsky, premieres at the Sundance Film Festival
timeline.significance: HBO documentary on the Waukesha case

timeline.event: Sony Pictures' Slender Man film opens in U.S. theaters

history.modern_era: Slender Man is now an established figure of digital folklore studied alongside earlier urban legends. The Waukesha case, in which both Geyser and Weier were tried as adults and committed to Wisconsin mental-health institutions, prompted ongoing debates about juvenile justice, mental illness, and the influence of internet-mediated belief on vulnerable young people.

photographic.name: Original Knudsen Slender Man photographs (June 10, 2009)
photographic.description: Two black-and-white photographs digitally composited by Eric Knudsen showing children with a tall, thin figure in a black suit added in the background.
photographic.analysis: Acknowledged fiction by their creator. Foundational images of the character.

video.name: Marble Hornets
video.description: Found-footage YouTube web series by Troy Wagner, Joseph DeLage, and Tim Sutton featuring the character as 'The Operator'.
video.analysis: Acknowledged fiction. Most influential video treatment of Slender Man.

documentary.name: Beware the Slenderman (HBO, 2016)
documentary.description: Documentary by Irene Taylor Brodsky examining the 2014 Waukesha stabbing and the role of internet folklore.
documentary.analysis: Standard documentary reference for the Waukesha case.

scientific.name: Digital folklore
scientific.description: Folklorists analyse Slender Man as an exemplar of internet-mediated folklore: collectively authored, performance-driven, and varying across communities — structurally similar to oral folklore, but using digital media.
evidence_cited: Collaborative authorship history on Something Awful, 4chan, and YouTube
Variation in lore across communities (ARG continuities)

skeptical.name: Acknowledged fiction
skeptical.description: The character is an acknowledged fictional creation by a known author; no independent evidence of any corresponding real entity exists.
evidence_cited: Knudsen's authorship of the original images

folklore.beliefs: Treated by adult communities as fiction; the Waukesha case demonstrates how some young people can come to treat fictional entities as real, with serious consequences.
